■ Problem Context

The University Exam Timetabling Crisis

Why traditional spreadsheets and manual scheduling collapse at university scale

1. Cross-Discipline Clashes

Modern credit-based systems enable cross-department electives (e.g. CSE majors taking Math, AI, or Physics minors). Manual scheduling frequently leads to concurrent exam clashes, student anxiety, and emergency re-examinations.

2. Campus Spatial Fragmentation

Collegiate campuses comprise hundreds of classrooms and labs across multiple blocks. Without intelligent floor-by-floor allocation, exam halls are either overcrowded or empty, causing severe logistics confusion on exam morning.

3. NP-Complete Bottleneck

Exam timetabling is an NP-complete combinatorial problem. Examination cells spend 2 to 3 weeks drafting tentative spreadsheets that are vulnerable to human oversight and last-minute student grievances.

Presenter Script: Today's university curriculum is highly modular. When universities schedule exams manually, our baseline tests revealed an 18% clash probability. We needed a deterministic mathematical model that provides zero-clash guarantees in milliseconds.
■ Mathematical Foundation

Welsh-Powell Graph Coloring Engine

Formulating academic scheduling as a chromatic number optimization problem

Conflict Graph G = (V, E, W)
  • Vertices V: Distinct course codes (52 courses across 8 branches).
  • Edges E: Undirected edge between Course A & Course B if any student is enrolled in both.
  • Weights W: Total number of shared students (quantifies conflict intensity).
  • Chromatic Number χ(G): The exact minimum number of colors (time slots) required so no adjacent courses share the same slot.
Welsh-Powell Execution Pipeline
  • 1. Degree Calculation: Compute deg(v) and sort vertices descending.
  • 2. Assign Initial Color: Color the highest-degree vertex with Slot k.
  • 3. Greedy Propagation: Color non-adjacent vertices in descending order with Slot k.
  • 4. Increment: Advance to Slot k+1 until all courses are colored.
  • Guarantee: Adjacent nodes never share colors ⟹ ZERO exam clashes!
Presenter Script: Graph coloring guarantees that any two courses sharing even a single student receive different time slots. Welsh-Powell achieves near-optimal chromatic coloring in polynomial time O(|V| log |V| + |E|), replacing exponential brute force.
■ Visual Proof

Conflict Graph & Chromatic Slot Proof

Visual proof of zero student clashes across connected course nodes

Algorithmic Insights
  • Independent Sets: All courses sharing a color form an independent set in G — meaning zero edges exist between them.
  • Color-Coded Slots: Blue = Slot 1, Red = Slot 2, Green = Slot 3, Amber = Slot 4.
  • High-Degree Anchors: Core foundational courses like Calculus (MAT2001) and Data Structures (CSE2001) are colored first.
  • Administrative Audit: Deans can visually verify schedule integrity by confirming no adjacent nodes share identical colors.
Presenter Script: In this diagram, each node is a course and each edge is a student overlap. Notice that adjacent nodes NEVER share the same color. Courses of the same color run simultaneously without a single student having a conflict.
■ Spatial Optimization

Campus Room Inventory & Greedy Bin-Packing

Allocating students across 208 rooms in Central Block, AB1, and AB2

Central Block (CB)

5 Floors • 80 Rooms
50 Classrooms @ 70 seats
30 Computer Labs @ 35 seats
Capacity: 4,550 seats (Primary allocation)

Academic Block 1 (AB1)

4 Floors • 64 Rooms
40 Classrooms @ 70 seats
24 Computer Labs @ 35 seats
Capacity: 3,640 seats (Secondary allocation)

Academic Block 2 (AB2)

4 Floors • 64 Rooms
40 Classrooms @ 70 seats
24 Computer Labs @ 35 seats
Capacity: 3,640 seats (Tertiary allocation)

Spatial Engine Features:

• Sequential Floor Packing: CB Floor 1→5, then AB1 1→4, then AB2 1→4 keeps branches clustered together.
• Strict Non-Overlapping Guarantee: Simultaneous courses get disjoint rooms.
• Invigilator Auto-Assignment: Computes 1 invigilator per room assigned (e.g. 42 rooms = 42 invigilators).

Presenter Script: Real universities need room assignments, not just time slots. We modeled 208 rooms across CB, AB1, and AB2 with 11,830 total seating capacity. Our bin-packing algorithm fills classrooms sequentially and automatically assigns invigilators.

■ System Architecture

Production 3-Tier Microservices Architecture

Modular full-stack engineering ensuring speed, reliability, and clear separation

Microservices Breakdown
  • React 18 Dashboard: Built with Vite, Vis.js canvas physics, Tailwind utility styling, and stateful tab navigation.
  • Node.js Gateway (Port 3001): CSV stream validation, row-level error reporting, ExcelJS 3-sheet workbook generator, and HTML templating.
  • Python Solver (Port 8000): FastAPI + NetworkX executing Welsh-Powell graph coloring and greedy spatial room bin-packing in <100ms.
  • Offline Mock Resilience: Evaluators can test full dashboard capabilities without running backend services!
Presenter Script: Our architecture is decoupled into 3 microservices: Python FastAPI for heavy graph computation, Node.js Express for file validation and Excel exports, and React 18 for graph visualization.

■ Frontend & UX

Interactive React Dashboard & Export Suite

Feature-rich administrative interface built specifically for university exam cells

1. Dynamic Graph Canvas (Vis.js)

Interactive physics simulation allowing administrators to zoom, drag, and inspect course clusters. Hovering over any node displays course name, student enrollment count, and connected conflict neighbors in real time.

2. Tabbed Timetable & Room View

Clean day-by-day timetable tabs (Day 1 Morning to Day 6 Afternoon). Shows concurrent courses, total students per slot, specific rooms assigned (e.g. CB-101, CB-102), and invigilator counts.

3. Pre-Flight CSV Validation

Client and gateway validation catches corrupt CSV formats, missing columns, duplicate enrollments, and invalid student IDs before sending payloads to the solver, providing line-by-line feedback.

4. Comprehensive Export Utility

1-click export generating an Excel workbook with 3 distinct sheets (Summary Metrics, Slot Timetable, Room Allocation Roster) as well as a printable, publication-ready HTML timetable.

Presenter Script: Our UI features an interactive graph physics canvas, tabbed timetable view, pre-flight data sanitization, and 1-click multi-sheet Excel and printable HTML exports.
